Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident and my injury, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where the accident happened?
A: It was on a multi-lane road in Pasadena, Texas, near a shopping plaza. I was in the middle lane heading toward
the freeway on-ramp.
Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I was changing lanes to the right because I needed to get over for the exit. I checked my mirror and signaled, and I
started to move over slowly.
Q: Did you notice the other vehicle?
A: Not at first. Then I heard a loud scrape and felt my car get pushed toward the curb. The other car had come up
alongside me on the right side.
Q: Did you see the other driver's signal or lights before you moved?
A: I didn't see any signal. I think they were in my blind spot and I just didn't catch them in time.
Q: Did you stop after the contact?
A: Yes, I pulled onto the shoulder right away. The other driver also stopped, and we exchanged information.
Q: Tell me about your injury.
A: My right knee hit the dashboard and the door frame when the car jolted. It swelled up within a few hours and it's
painful to bend or put weight on it.
Q: Have you received medical treatment for the knee?
A: Yes, I was seen at an urgent care clinic that same evening. They took X-rays and told me to follow up with a
specialist.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. Stairs are hard, and I've had to limit my driving and work sihfts while it heals.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I was trying to drive carefully and I want my knee looked after properly. That's everything I have.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
